To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the design of computational media must be informed by a theory of human culture and the nature of human creativity, and (b) the design of media for learning and collaboration should be informed by theories and models of learning and collaborative work.

(1) the media we use shape the way we think; (2) we can use the media we design to change our thinking and our cultures; and (3) we need to design media that support our thinking and cultures in ways that we do not yet know how to specify, because the media will be designed to support the thinking and cultures that will emerge from the use of the media.

(1) the design of computational media can contribute to the invention of new cultures; (2) new media and new cultures are mutually dependent; and (3) the invention of new media and new culture requires the active engagement and contribution of users.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of media that can help to shape our cultures.
the development of computational media that support the invention and evolution of cultures in which people are active designers and contributors.
the development of new media for new cultures, which will be more open, more participatory, more creative, more democratic, and more sustainable.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
new media can change the very nature of our minds.
the fundamental challenge for computational science and media is to invent and design new cultures.
new media change the way we think, work and play.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fundamental challenge for computational science and media is to contribute the invention and design, of cultures in which we can express ourselves and engage in personally meaning activities.
we have developed and applied new computational media for thinking, working and learning, and for the design of new media for thinking, learning and working.
we are interested in how we can design media that enable people to express themselves, to collaborate, to think and to learn, and how this can lead to new cultures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
computational media are a new kind of tool that is not only a medium, but also a means to design new media.
computational media are not merely tools for the expression and exchange of ideas, but are a fundamental medium of human experience and thought.
computational media should be developed with a focus on supporting the invention of new cultures, and not just the design of new media.
